verdict.rationale: Turso ships an official MCP server that lets any MCP-capable agent manage the account and run SQL (turso-docs-9/37, turso-probe-4), and separately offers fine-grained, per-token permission scoping by database/table/action (turso-docs-56, turso-docs-57) which could underlie safe delegation. But there is no documentation showing the MCP server's own tool set explicitly separates read-only vs destructive operations (e.g., a distinct 'query' vs 'execute-destructive' tool), so the specific safety-scoping claim in the story is only inferentially supported. missing for 10: explicit MCP tool-level read-only/destructive distinction, documentation or examples showing agents blocked from destructive ops by default, independent/hands-on confirmation of this safety behavior.
